finding.expected: Preserve the existing canonical REPAIR/reuse authority instead of inferring Executor need from `NO_CHANGE` alone. A non-qualifying ordinary NO_CHANGE REPAIR with no explicit Human Executor must return bounded `EXECUTOR_REQUIRED` before delegation, RUN creation, or Admission Failure persistence; an actually eligible TASK-064 verification-only continuation must invoke zero coding Executors without silently selecting/defaulting a coding Executor as Human authority, while keeping frozen RUN/lineage truth explicit. Delegated operation success and failure must remain one-operation-only and produce the bounded versioned Human-surface outcome required by TASK-087, while the existing Admission Failure v2 or RUN FAILURE remains the sole canonical failure artifact and no retry, reroute, duplicate failure authority, or second operation is introduced. Add focused regressions covering qualifying versus non-qualifying NO_CHANGE and delegated pre-RUN versus admitted failure behavior, preserving all existing low-level command semantics.
finding.issue: The unified Human surface does not yet preserve exact Executor authority and bounded outcome semantics across REPAIR and failure paths. `continue_task` decides that every `EXECUTE_REPAIR` whose preflight reports action `NO_CHANGE` needs no Executor, but the TASK-085 preflight result exposes only the authorized action, not whether TASK-064 reusable pre-verification state actually qualified. TASK-064 explicitly requires a non-qualifying NO_CHANGE REPAIR to retain the ordinary one-Executor path. With no `--executor`, such a READY NO_CHANGE state is therefore delegated into `run_repair`, which only later discovers `reusable_package is None` and raises; the Human receives a canonical REPAIR Admission Failure instead of the required non-delegated `EXECUTOR_REQUIRED` outcome. Conversely, when reuse is eligible and no Executor was supplied, `run_repair` fabricates `run_executor = "codex"`, so the canonical RUN and summary identify an Executor that the Human did not select even though this surface is forbidden to default, infer, or silently reuse one. Finally, delegated canonical operation exceptions escape `continue_task`; `main` falls back to plain `AIOS ERROR` and emits no versioned `AIOS_HUMAN_SURFACE` result for that delegated outcome, leaving the failure-facing part of AC9/AC11 and the README claim of one bounded Human result unfulfilled.
finding.location: src/aios_renew/operator.py::continue_task / run_repair / main Human-surface delegation boundary
